name: held mark from recorded metadata
claim: The turn profile marks a call or a turn held only from what the harness recorded about a hold (x.held on the tool message, stop reason held), never from words in message or result text.

models.result: scripts/test-profile.mjs: 8 held checks, 6 red at 1f0f366, green at 924864a: profile 78/78, validators 46/46. Fixtures are metadata only: one session with 2 held calls and a held stop, one whose repo text says held and approval with no hold (4 ok, 0 held). Gap left: the harness does not yet write x.held when a call waits at a hold, so real held calls show as ok until it does. Saved H12 sessions not re-run: only their profiles are in the repo.

held mark written by the page: red 7 of 13 held mark checks at eaed07d (6 guards green), green 13 of 13 at b95087d; smoke 291 pass, 0 fail. x.held is true on the tool message of a call that waited at a hold, released or skipped; no held key at all on a call that never waited (pace run, nameless, scope-refused). Model view unchanged (x is stripped in app/context.js; fixtures *-pre-aa62df3 and the held call assertion still pass); the mark survives session save and load, and the profile counts both held calls. Not measured with a real model.

fault: the turn profile classed a tool result as held when the word held, or approval, appeared in its first 120 characters; repository text printed by git log or cat was then counted as a held call
handled: resultClass has no held class; profile() marks a call held only from x.held on its tool message, a turn held only from stop reason held (924864a). The harness now writes x.held when a call waits at a hold, released or skipped, and no key on a call that never waited (app/main.js turnsInner / hold, b95087d), so the held class counts real held calls from sessions run on that commit; earlier sessions read as ok. The old text rule never matched a real hold, so removing it lost no true marks.
